dimensionScore.description: For each dimension, score = (number of times a statement from this dimension was chosen) / (number of times it was offered).
dimensionScore.timesOffered: count of items (id 1-100 only, excluding control items) where statementA.dimension == code OR statementB.dimension == code
dimensionScore.timesChosen: count of items where the chosen side's statement.dimension == code

consistencyCheck.description: For each control item (id 101-110), compare the answer given to the item with the same id as controlOf. Consistency score = matches / 10.

responsePatternCheck.description: Share of 'A' answers among items 1-100 (control items excluded). Flag if outside 0.15-0.85 (under-differentiated / careless responding).

report.description: Narrative report generator: for each dimension, pick the band ('Low' if dimensionScore < 0.4, 'Mid' if <= 0.6, else 'High') and use report[code].bands[band] as the paragraph, plus the static strengths/suitableWork/tips lines. For the overall summary: if (max dimension score - min dimension score) < 0.25, use a 'balanced profile' message; otherwise name the dimension with the max score as dominant and the one with the min score as weakest.

bands.Low: You're comfortable in a supporting role and prefer letting someone else make the final call. You engage actively once the framework is set, but don't feel a systematic need to lead. This eases collaboration, but in an emergency requiring a fast, solo decision you may tend to wait for outside validation before acting.
bands.Mid: You take charge when the situation calls for it, without needing to lead constantly. You naturally alternate between leading and following depending on context, which helps you adapt to the group's dynamics.
bands.High: You naturally take the initiative and structure the action when a decision needs to be made. This ease with leading is an asset in a crisis, but it can also lead you to decide a bit too fast or consult your crew less if you're not paying attention.

LEAD.strengths: You know how to structure the action and reassure a crew in uncertain moments.
LEAD.suitableWork: Roles requiring fast decision-making and team coordination (captain, instructor, mission lead).
LEAD.tips: Keep seeking your crew's input before deciding, even when you're confident in your call.

bands.Low: You're comfortable acting independently and don't necessarily rely on group validation to move forward. This independence is an asset solo, but in a crew setting it can translate into less spontaneous information-sharing if you're not attentive to it.
bands.Mid: You balance independent work with consulting your crew. You involve others when the situation calls for it, without losing individual efficiency.
bands.High: You place great importance on building decisions collectively and on group cohesion. That's a strong CRM asset, but be careful not to over-rely on others' validation in situations that require fast individual action.

TEAM.strengths: Your team spirit fosters cohesion and trust within the crew.
TEAM.suitableWork: Collaborative environments where crew/pair work is central.
TEAM.tips: Practice acting fast and alone in situations that require it, without systematically waiting for group validation.

bands.Low: You tend to keep reservations to yourself rather than voice them systematically, especially with an authority figure. That's a quality of discretion, but in aviation an unexpressed doubt can have safety consequences.
bands.Mid: You voice your opinion when necessary, while calibrating your candor to the context and the person you're speaking with.
bands.High: You clearly say what you think, including when disagreeing with a superior. That's a major CRM/safety asset, provided you keep the phrasing constructive so as not to put the other person on the defensive.

COM.strengths: Your ability to clearly voice observations is a direct safety asset.
COM.suitableWork: Roles requiring active CRM and frequent communication with management or air traffic control.
COM.tips: Work on assertive but non-confrontational phrasing for delivering a sensitive message.

bands.Low: You favor substance over form and can adapt to a less strict framework. This flexibility eases adaptation, but in a job where procedures underpin safety, it calls for particular vigilance around systematically following checklists.
bands.Mid: You follow procedures seriously while keeping an ability to adapt when context requires it.
bands.High: You're rigorous, methodical, attentive to detail. That's a clear safety asset, provided this thoroughness doesn't translate into excessive time loss in situations that call for quick reaction.

RIG.strengths: Your thoroughness in following procedures is a pillar of operational safety.
RIG.suitableWork: Any technical role where strict procedure compliance matters (flying, maintenance, quality control).
RIG.tips: Make sure you keep enough reaction time even when a full checklist takes a while.

bands.Low: You may be more sensitive than average to tense situations, which makes you particularly attuned to weak signals. Working on stress-management techniques could help you gain composure during high-workload moments.
bands.Mid: You handle pressure well in most situations, with an occasional need to catch your breath before deciding.
bands.High: You stay calm and clear-headed even under heavy pressure — a valuable asset in emergencies. Be careful, though, not to underestimate your own fatigue or stress simply because you don't show outward signs of it.

STR.strengths: Your clarity of mind under pressure is a direct asset in emergency management.
STR.suitableWork: High-workload or high-stakes decision roles (line flying, instruction, crisis management).
STR.tips: Practice breathing or mental-preparation exercises to further strengthen your stress management.

bands.Low: You value stability and familiar reference points. You do adapt, but need a bit more time than average to absorb a last-minute change.
bands.Mid: You adjust to the unexpected without major difficulty, while still preferring a minimum of structure.
bands.High: You adapt quickly to the unexpected and bounce back easily when plans change. This agility is valuable operationally, provided you don't under-invest in upfront preparation.

ADA.strengths: Your agility in the face of the unexpected lets you bounce back quickly operationally.
ADA.suitableWork: Changing environments (long-haul, varied rotations, multicultural contexts).
ADA.tips: Keep a minimum of preparation structure so you don't under-invest in anticipation.

bands.Low: You may doubt your judgment more when it's challenged, which makes you receptive to others' feedback — a useful trait of humility, provided it doesn't hold back your own autonomous decision-making.
bands.Mid: You generally trust your judgment while still being able to question it when needed.
bands.High: You have solid confidence in your decisions and aren't easily shaken by criticism. That's a stability asset, provided you stay open to feedback that could nuance your position.

CONF.strengths: Your psychological stability reassures the crew in difficult moments.
CONF.suitableWork: Leadership, instruction, or high-stakes situation management roles.
CONF.tips: Stay open to conflicting feedback, even when your conviction is strong.

bands.Low: In some contexts you may favor the simplest or fastest solution over the one most rigorous on safety. This is worth working on, since consistently prioritizing safety is a fundamental of the job.
bands.Mid: You generally put safety and integrity at the heart of your decisions, with good awareness of collective stakes.
bands.High: You consistently place safety and ethics above any other consideration, including commercial ones. That's an essential strength in this profession.

RESP.strengths: Your integrity and consistent prioritization of safety are a solid foundation for this profession.
RESP.suitableWork: Any aviation role, particularly those exposed to commercial pressure (line, charter).
RESP.tips: Keep documenting and reporting systematically, even minor deviations with no visible consequence.

bands.Low: You generally prefer acting within a framework already set by others rather than originating initiatives yourself. This can be an asset in a highly procedural environment, but calls for vigilance around stepping up when the situation requires it.
bands.Mid: You act autonomously when necessary, without needing to initiate everything yourself.
bands.High: You easily take the lead and don't wait for detailed instructions to act. This autonomy is an asset, provided you stay well synchronized with the rest of the crew.

AUTO.strengths: Your ability to act without waiting for detailed instructions is a real gain in responsiveness.
AUTO.suitableWork: High individual-responsibility roles (captain, instructor, solo post).
AUTO.tips: Make sure your initiatives stay well synchronized with the rest of the team to avoid siloed decisions.

bands.Low: You may feel fatigue sooner than average on long days or dense rotations. Paying particular attention to rest and recovery would be a useful area for improvement.
bands.Mid: You generally hold up well on demanding workdays, with good energy management.
bands.High: You maintain a high level of alertness and motivation even at the end of a duty period or on dense rotations. A robust asset, provided you stay attuned to early fatigue signals despite this apparent resilience.

END.strengths: Your endurance over time is an asset for long, demanding rotations.
END.suitableWork: Long-haul, high-workload rotations, missions with frequent time-zone changes.
END.tips: Watch for early fatigue signals despite your good apparent resilience — sleep hygiene still matters.
